source_text: Qui vero non hic, id est, non intra hunc ambitum terrae, nec per hunc commeatum vitae, nec apud homines hujus naturae communis confessionem putant constitutam, quanta praesumptio est adversus omnem ordinem rerum in terris istis, et in vita ista, et sub humanis potestatibus experiundarum? Nimirum cum animae de corporibus excesserint, et per singula tabulata coelorum de praecepto dispici coeperint, et interrogari arcana illa haereticorum sacramenta, tunc confitendum apud veras potestates et veros homines, Theletos scilicet et Abascantos et Acinetos Valentini. Nostrates enim, inquiunt, nec ipse Demiurgus constanter homines probabat veros esse, quos stillicidium situlae et pulverem areae et sputamen et locustas deputavit; etiam irrationalibus jumentis adaequavit. Plane ita scriptum. Non tamen idcirco aliud hominis genus intelligendum praeter nos: quos quia constat esse, et comparatione potuit induere, salva et proprietate generis, et singularitate. Neque enim si vita vitiata est, ut despectui judicata despectis compararetur, statim natura sublata est, ut alia in nomine ejus deputaretur. Atquin servatur natura, etsi suffunditur vita, nec alios novit Christus homines, quam de quibus dicit: Quem me aiunt esse homines? et: Quomodo vultis ut faciant vobis homines, et ita vos facite illis. Vide an servaverit genus, a quibus et testimonium sui exspectet, et in quos justitiae vicem mandat. Illos autem coelestes homines si expostulem mihi ostendi, facilius Aratus Persea, et Cephea, et Erigonam, et Ariadnam inter sidera deliniabit. Quis autem prohibuit Dominum illic etiam confessionem hominum faciendam manifeste determinare, ubi suam futuram aperte pronuntiavit? ut ita esset positum: «Qui in me confessus fuerit coram hominibus in coelis, et ego in illo confitebor coram Patre meo qui in coelis est?» Eripere me debuit ex isto terrenae confessionis errore, quam suscipi noluit, si coelestem praecepisset, quia nullos alios homines noveram praeter incolas terrae; ne ipso quidem adhuc tunc in coelis homine conspecto. Quae porro fides rerum, ut post excessum ad superna sublevatus, illic probarer, quo non nisi jam probatus imponerer? illic de praecepto examinarer, quo nisi admittendus pervenire non possem? Christiano coelum ante patet quam via; quia nulla via in coelum, nisi cui patet coelum; quod qui attigerit, intrabit. Quas mihi potestates janitrices affirmas juxta romanam superstitionem Janum quemdam et Forculum et Limentinum? quas a cancellis ordinas potestates? Si unquam legisti apud David, auferte portas principes vestras, et subleventur portae aeternae, et intrabit rex gloriae. Si item audisti apud Amos: Qui assensum illum suum aedificat in coelos, et profusionem suam fundat in terras; scito et ascensum illum exinde complanatum vestigiis Domini, et introitum exinde reseratum viribus Christi, nec ullam moram aut quaestionem in limine Christianis occursuram, qui non dignosci habeant illic, sed agnosci; nec interrogari, sed admitti. Nam et si adhuc clausum putas coelum, memento claves ejus hic Dominum Petro, et per eum, Ecclesiae reliquisse, quas hic unusquisque interrogatus atque confessus feret secum. Sed asseverat diabolus illic confitendum, ut suadeat hic negandum. Pulchra videlicet documenta praemittam, bonas mecum claves feram, timorem eorum, qui solum corpus occidunt, animae autem nihil faciunt: commendatus ero hujus praecepti desertione; honeste in coelestibus stabo, qui in terrenis stare non potui; sustinebo majores potestates, qui minoribus cessi; merebor denique admitti, jam exclusus. Suppetit adhuc dicere: si in coelestibus confitendum, et hic negandum est; nam ubi alterum, ibi utrumque; aemula enim quaeque concurrunt. Etiam persecutionem in coelis agitari oportebit, quae confessionis negationisve materia est. Quid itaque cessas, audacissime haeretice, totum ordinem christianae concussionis in superna transferre, et in primis, ipsum nominis odium illic collocare, ubi ad Patris dexteram praesidet Christus? Illic constitues et synagogas Judaeorum, fontes persecutionum, apud quas Apostoli flagella perpessi sunt, et populos nationum cum suo quidem circo, ubi facile conclamant, «Usquequo genus tertium?» Sed et fratres nostros et patres et filios et socrus et nurus et domesticos nostros ibidem exhibere debebis, per quos traditio disposita est: item reges et praesides et armatas potestates, apud quos caussa purganda est. Erit certe etiam carcer in coelo, carens sole, aut ingratis luminosus, et vincula fortasse de zonis, et equuleus axis ipse qui torquet: tum si lapidandus christianus, grandines aderunt; si urendus, fulmina prae manu sunt; si trucidandus, Orionis armati manus operabitur; si bestiis finiendus, ursas septemtrio emittet, zodiacus tauros et leones. Haec qui sustinuerit in finem, iste erit salvus. Ergone et finis in coelis, et passio, et occisio, et prima confessio? Et ubi caro, omnibus istis necessaria? ubi corpus? quod solum ab hominibus habet occidi. Haec nobis etiam ludicrum in modum certa ratio mandavit, nec ullus obicem praescriptionis istius extrudet, ut non omnem ordinem persecutionis, omnem ejus caussae firmam paraturam illuc transferre cogatur, ubi confessioni forum dederit. Siquidem confessio a persecutione deducitur, et persecutio in confessione finitur. Nec possunt non una sequi, quae et aditum et exitum, id est, initium finemque disponunt. Porro et odium nominis hic erit, et persecutio hic erumpit, et traditio hic producit, et interrogatio hic compellit, et carnificina hic desaevit, et totum hunc ordinem in terris confessio vel negatio expungit. Igitur si caetera hic, nec confessio alibi; si confessio alibi, nec caetera hic. Enimvero non alibi caetera; itaque nec confessio in coelo. Aut si aliam volunt esse rationem interrogationis et confessionis coelestis, utique et ordinem suum illi struere debebunt alium longe, et ab ista dispositione diversum, quae Scripturis notatur, et possumus dicere, Viderint, dum hic ordo terrenae interrogationis et confessionis, ex materia decurrens persecutionis et discordiae publicae in nomen, salvus sit suae fidei; ut ita credendum sit sicut et scribitur, ita intelligendum sit sicuti auditur. Hic omnem ordinem sustineo, ipso Domino non aliam regionem mundi destinante. Quid enim post confessionis et negationis terminum subjungit? Ne putaveritis venisse me uti pacem mittam in terram; non veni, sed ut machaeram, certe in terram. Veni enim dividere hominem adversus patrem suum, et filiam adversus matrem suam, et socrum adversus nurum suam: et inimici homini domestici sui. Sic enim efficitur, ut tradat frater fratrem in mortem, et pater filium, et insurgant filii in parentes, et mori eos faciant. Et qui sustinuerit in finem, hic salvus erit. Adeo totus hic ordo dominicae machaerae, non in coelum missae, sed in terram, illic constituit etiam confessionem, quae in finem sustinendo passura est mortem.
pass_a_gloss: But who indeed not here, that is, not within this circle of the earth, nor through this journey of life, nor among men of this common nature think that confession is established, what presumption is it against all order of things on these earths, and in this life, and under human powers to be experienced? For when souls have gone out from bodies, and through individual levels of the heavens have begun to be examined by command, and to be questioned about those secret heretical sacraments, then it must be confessed among true powers and true men, namely Theletos and Abascantos and Acinetos of Valentinus. For our people, they say, not even the Demiurge himself consistently proved men to be true, whom he assigned to be like the dripping of a bucket and the dust of a threshing floor and spittle and locusts; and he also made them equal to irrational beasts. Plainly it is written. Nevertheless, not for this reason is another kind of man to be understood apart from us: whom because it is agreed that they exist, and by comparison could have been induced, with the nature of the kind and the singularity preserved. For if life is corrupted, so that it may be judged to be despised in comparison with the despised, nature is not immediately abolished, so that another may be substituted in its name. But nature is preserved, even if life is corrupted, and Christ does not know other men than those about whom he says: 'Whom do men say that I am?' and 'How do you want men to do to you, and so you do to them.' See whether he preserved the kind, from whom he also expects testimony of himself, and in whom he commands the duty of justice. But if I were to demand that those heavenly men be shown to me, Aratus would more easily depict Perseus and Cepheus and Erigone and Ariadne among the stars. For who prohibited the Lord from determining there also that a confession of men should be made manifest, where he openly proclaimed that his own would be in the future? So that it might be said: 'Whoever has confessed me before men on earth, I will also confess him before my Father who is in heaven.' He ought to have rescued me from this error of earthly confession, which he did not want to receive, if he had commanded a heavenly one, because I knew no other men apart from the inhabitants of the earth; not even the man in heaven was yet seen by me. What faith is there in things, so that after passing away I might be lifted up to the things above, and there be approved, to which I could not be introduced unless already approved? There I would be examined by command, to which I could not arrive unless admitted. For the Christian, heaven lies open before the way; because there is no way to heaven, unless heaven lies open; which whoever has touched, will enter. What powers do you affirm to me as doorkeepers, according to the Roman superstition, a certain Janus and Forculus and Limentinus? What powers do you arrange at the gates? If you have ever read in David, 'Remove your gates, princes, and the eternal gates will be lifted up, and the king of glory will enter.' If also you have heard in Amos: 'Who builds his ascent to the heavens, and founds his abundance on the earth;' know also that the ascent from there is made level by the footsteps of the Lord, and the entrance from there is opened by the powers of Christ, and no delay or questioning will occur to Christians at the threshold, who are not to be distinguished there, but recognized; not to be questioned, but admitted. For even if you think that heaven is still closed, remember that the Lord left its keys here to Peter, and through him, to the rest of the Church, which each one, having been questioned and confessed, will carry with him. But the devil asserts that confession must be made there, so that he may persuade us to deny it here. Beautiful documents will I present beforehand, good keys will I bring with me, fear of those who can only kill the body, but do nothing to the soul; I will be commended for the abandonment of this command; I will stand honorably in the heavenly places, who could not stand on earth; I will endure greater powers, who yielded to lesser ones; I will finally deserve to be admitted, now that I have been excluded. It is still possible to say: if confession is to be made in heaven, and denial here; for where one is, the other is also; for rival things run together. Also, persecution will have to be stirred up in heaven, which is the material for confession or denial. Why then do you hesitate, most audacious heretic, to transfer the entire order of Christian agitation to the heavenly places, and first of all, to establish the hatred of the name there, where Christ presides at the right hand of the Father? There you will establish the synagogues of the Jews, the sources of persecutions, among whom the Apostles suffered beatings, and the peoples of the nations with their own circus, where they easily shout, 'How long until the third kind?' But you ought also to exhibit our brothers and fathers and sons and mothers-in-law and daughters-in-law and our household members there, through whom the tradition is arranged; also kings and presidents and armed powers, among whom the case is to be purified. There will certainly also be a prison in heaven, lacking the sun, or shining with unpleasant light, and chains perhaps made of straps, and a rack which is the axis itself that twists; then if a Christian is to be stoned, hailstones will be at hand; if he is to be burned, lightning will be before him; if he is to be killed, the armed hands of Orion will work; if he is to be thrown to the beasts, the seven stars will send forth bears, and the zodiac will send forth bulls and lions. He who will have endured these things to the end, this one will be saved. Therefore, is the end also in heaven, and passion, and killing, and first confession? And where is the flesh, necessary for all these things? Where is the body, which alone can be killed by men? This certain reason has commanded us, even in a playful manner, and no one will push away the objection of this prescription, so that we are not forced to transfer the entire order of persecution, the entire firm preparation of its case, to the place where we have given a forum to confession. For if confession is derived from persecution, and persecution ends in confession, they cannot but follow one another, since they arrange both the beginning and the end, that is, the entrance and exit. Furthermore, the hatred of the name will be here, and persecution will break out here, and tradition will produce here, and questioning will compel here, and carnage will rage here, and the entire order of confession or denial will be destroyed on earth. Therefore, if the other things are here, confession is not elsewhere; if confession is elsewhere, the other things are not here. For the other things are not elsewhere; therefore, confession is not in heaven. Or if they want to be another reason for heavenly questioning and confession, they will certainly have to construct another order for it, far different from this arrangement, which is noted in the Scriptures, and we can say, 'Let them see to it,' while the order of earthly questioning and confession, flowing from the material of persecution and public discord in the name, is preserved safe in its faith; so that it is to be believed as it is written, and understood as it is heard. I sustain the entire order here, the Lord himself not designating another region of the world. For what does he add after the end of confession and denial? 'Do not think that I have come to bring peace on earth; I have not come to bring peace, but a sword, certainly on earth.' For I have come to divide a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law; and a man's enemies will be those of his own household. For thus it happens that a brother hands over his brother to death, and a father his son, and sons rise up against their parents, and make them die. And he who will have endured to the end, this one will be saved. So great is the entire order of the Lord's sword, not sent into heaven, but into earth, which also establishes confession there, which will suffer death by enduring to the end.

pass_b_english: What colossal presumption against the whole order of things on this earth, in this life, and under these human powers—things meant to be experienced—drives anyone who thinks confession is not established here, within this circle of the earth, nor through this journey of life, nor among men of this common nature? For when souls have left their bodies and begun to be examined by command through the successive levels of the heavens, and to be interrogated about those secret heretical sacraments, then confession must be made before the true powers and the true men—namely Theletos, Abascantos, and Acinetos of Valentinus. They claim our people were not even consistently proven true men by the Demiurge himself, who assigned them to be the dripping of a bucket, the dust of a threshing floor, spittle, and locusts, and even equated them with irrational beasts. True, it is written that way. Yet that is no reason to understand another kind of man besides us—men whose existence is agreed upon, and whom comparison could have fitted out while preserving both the property of the kind and its singularity. For if life is corrupted, so that it is judged contemptible by comparison with the contemptible, nature is not instantly abolished so that another might be substituted in its name. But nature is preserved even if life is corrupted, and Christ knows no other men than those about whom he says, 'Who do men say that I am?' (Matt. 16:13) and 'Whatever you wish that men would do to you, do so to them' (Matt. 7:12). See whether he preserved the kind from whom he also expects testimony about himself and in whom he commands the duty of justice. If I were to demand that those heavenly men be shown to me, Aratus would more easily trace Perseus, Cepheus, Erigone, and Ariadne among the stars. Who, after all, prevented the Lord from determining right there that a confession of men should be made manifest, where he openly proclaimed that his own future confession would be? So that it might be put: 'Whoever confesses me before men on earth, I also will confess before my Father who is in heaven' (Matt. 10:32). He ought to have rescued me from this error of earthly confession, which he refused to accept, if he had commanded a heavenly one—since I knew no other men except the inhabitants of the earth; not even the man in heaven had yet been seen by me. What faith is there in things, that after I pass away and am lifted up to the heights I might be approved there—approved, that is, before I can even be introduced? There I would be examined by command, to which I could not arrive unless already admitted. For the Christian, heaven lies open before the way; because there is no way to heaven unless heaven lies open, and whoever touches it will enter. What powers do you affirm to me as doorkeepers, according to Roman superstition—a certain Janus, Forculus, and Limentinus? What powers do you station at the gates? If you have ever read in David, 'Lift up your heads, O gates! And be lifted up, O ancient doors, that the King of glory may come in' (Ps. 24:7,9). If you have also heard in Amos, 'Who builds his upper chambers in the heavens and founds his vault upon the earth' (Amos 9:6), know that the ascent from there is leveled by the footsteps of the Lord, and the entrance from there is opened by the powers of Christ, and no delay or questioning will meet Christians at the threshold—those who are not to be distinguished there, but recognized; not to be interrogated, but admitted. For even if you still think heaven is closed, remember the Lord left its keys here to Peter, and through him to the Church, which each one, having been questioned and confessed, will carry with him. But the devil asserts that confession must be made there, so that he may persuade us to deny it here. Lovely credentials I would present in advance, fine keys I would bring with me—the fear of those who kill only the body but can do nothing to the soul (Matt. 10:28); I would be commended for abandoning this command; I would stand honorably in the heavenly places, I who could not stand on earth; I would endure greater powers, I who yielded to lesser ones; I would finally deserve to be admitted, now that I am excluded. One can still say: if confession is to be made in heaven and denial here, for where one is, the other is also, since rival things run together. Persecution would also have to be stirred up in heaven, which is the material of confession or denial. So why do you hesitate, most audacious heretic, to transfer the entire order of Christian upheaval to the heavenly realms—and first of all to plant the hatred of the name there, where Christ presides at the right hand of the Father? There you will set up the synagogues of the Jews, the fountains of persecutions, among whom the apostles suffered beatings, and the nations' peoples with their own circus, where they easily shout, 'How long until the third kind?' But you must also exhibit our brothers and fathers and sons and mothers-in-law and daughters-in-law and our household members there, through whom tradition is handed down; likewise kings and governors and armed powers, before whom the case is to be cleared. There will certainly be a prison in heaven too, lacking the sun or shining with ungrateful light, and chains perhaps made of straps, and a rack which is the very axis that twists; then if a Christian is to be stoned, hailstones will be at hand; if to be burned, lightning will be ready; if to be slaughtered, the armed hands of Orion will do the work; if to be finished off by beasts, the Great Bear will send forth bears, the zodiac bulls and lions. He who endures these to the end, this one will be saved (Matt. 10:22; 24:13; Mark 13:13). So the end is in heaven too, and passion, and killing, and first confession? And where is the flesh, necessary for all these? Where is the body, which alone can be killed by men? This reasoning has commanded us, as it were in sport, and no one will shove aside the objection of this prescription, so that we are not forced to transfer the whole order of persecution, the whole firm preparation of its case, to the place where we have given confession a forum. For confession is derived from persecution, and persecution ends in confession; they cannot but follow each other, since they arrange both the entrance and the exit, that is, the beginning and the end. Moreover, the hatred of the name will be here, and persecution will break out here, and tradition will produce here, and questioning will compel here, and carnage will rage here, and the whole order of confession or denial will be wiped out on earth. Therefore, if the other things are here, confession is not elsewhere; if confession is elsewhere, the other things are not here. But the other things are not elsewhere; therefore confession is not in heaven. Or if they want a different rationale for heavenly interrogation and confession, they will certainly have to construct another order for it, far different from this arrangement which is marked in the Scriptures, and we can say, 'Let them see to it,' while the order of earthly interrogation and confession, flowing from the material of persecution and public discord in the name, remains secure in its faith—so that it is to be believed as it is written, and understood as it is heard. I sustain the whole order here, the Lord himself not designating another region of the world. For what does he add after the terminus of confession and denial? 'Do not think that I have come to bring peace on earth; I have not come to bring peace, but a sword, certainly on earth' (Matt. 10:34). 'For I have come to set a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; and a man's enemies will be those of his own household' (Matt. 10:35–36). 'And so it happens that a brother will deliver his brother to death, and a father his child, and children will rise against parents and have them put to death' (Matt. 10:21). 'And he who endures to the end, this one will be saved' (Matt. 10:22; 24:13; Mark 13:13). Such is the whole order of the Lord's sword, not sent into heaven but into earth, which also establishes confession there, where it will suffer death by enduring to the end.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. All clauses, including the complex theological arguments regarding the Demiurge and the nature of confession, are preserved. Scripture citations in Pass B (Matt. 16:13, Matt. 7:12, Matt. 10:32, Ps. 24:7,9, Amos 9:6, Matt. 10:28, Matt. 10:34, Matt. 10:35–36, Matt. 10:21, Matt. 10:22, 24:13, Mark 13:13) correctly identify the verses alluded to in the Latin (e.g., 'Quem me aiunt esse homines?' to Matt 16:13; 'Qui assensum illum suum...' to Amos 9:6). The translation of 'in terris istis' as 'on these earths' and 'tabulata coelorum' as 'levels of the heavens' maintains fidelity to the source.
